name: Shu Ping
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2012-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2018-2025)
forbes_bio: Shu Ping is a cofounder of Chinese hot pot chain Haidilao International Holding.
Shu and three friends, including Zhang Yong who became her husband and is now chairman and CEO of the company, set up their first restaurant with personal savings in 1994.
Haidilao has nearly 1,400 restaurants in Greater China. It is renowned for its spicy dishes and attentive customer service, including free manicures for waiting customers.
It spun off its overseas business Super Hi, which went public in Hong Kong in 2022 and had a dual listing on Nasdaq in 2024. Super Hi has over 120 restaurants in international markets.
Shu became chairman of Super Hi in 2023.

name: William Lauder
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: William Lauder is a grandson of Estée Lauder, who founded the cosmetics firm, and eldest son of Leonard Lauder, who was CEO and chairman for 17 years.
A member of the family's third generation, he was Estée Lauder's CEO from 2004 to 2009.
In January 2025, he stepped down as executive chairman of the company, a position he'd held since 2009.
He now serves as chairman of Estée Lauder's board of directors.
He lives in a Park Avenue co-op, and has homes in New York's Westchester County and in Aspen, Colorado.
forbes_facts: Lauder graduated from the University of Pennsylvania and now sits on the institution's board. He started lecturing Penn MBA students in 2012.
Lauder joined family's cosmetics company Estee Lauder in 1986 as regional marketing director of Clinique USA. He created the Origins brand in 1990.

name: Banwari Lal Bawri
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025)
forbes_bio: Banwari Lal Bawri is the joint managing director of privately held Macleods Pharmaceuticals, one of India's leading pharma firms.
Bawri, whose family owned a pharmacy in Jaipur, set up Macleods Pharmaceuticals with two siblings in 1986 to make anti-TB medicines.
Macleods produces generics for a range of diseases including asthma, osteoporosis and diabetes.
Older brother Girdharilal Bawri is chairman of Macleods. While younger brother Rajendra Agarwal passed away in November 2025.
forbes_facts: Bawri and his two brothers live together with their families in the same building in Mumbai.
The company was named after John Macleod, a Scottish doctor and author of medical textbooks.

forbes_bio: Huang Dawen derives his fortune from a stake in Shanghai-listed Hoshine Silicon Industry.
Huang is also the vice chairman of Ningbo Hoshine Apparel.
Hoshine Silicon Industry makes silicon and silicon-related products in China.

name: Eduard Kucera
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Eduard Kučera is the cofounder of Prague-based internet security company Avast Software.
In 1988, he and Pavel Baudis, with whom he'd worked at Research Institute of Mathematical Machines, cofounded ALWIL to sell an antivirus software.
Following the fall of Communism in 1989, the pair broke off to establish what would become Avast.
Now run by an outside CEO, Avast, which secures online activities for more than 435 million users, went public in 2018.
In 2021, Avast, which Kučera chaired Avast from 2006 to 2014, agreed to merge with cybersecurity firm NortonLifeLock.
forbes_facts: Kučera is one of the biggest watch collectors in Czechia; he also owns a significant vintage car collection with his son.

name: Chen Wenyuan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Wenyuan chairs HYC Technology, a supplier of testing equipment for LCD, semiconductor and new energy electronics businesses.
HYC listed on China's new STAR market for innovative companies on the Shanghai Stock Exchange on July 22, 2019
His wife Zhang Qian cofounded the predecessor business of HYC in 2005.

name: Ricardo Villela Marino
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Ricardo Villela Marino is a member of a storied Brazilian banking dynasty.
He is grandson of Eudoro Libânio Villela, who cofounded Brazilian bank Itau in 1945; it merged with Unibanco in 2008.
Ricardo Villela Marino is a partner and vice chairman of Itaú Unibanco and chairman of the bank's Latin America Strategic Council.
His mother, Maria de Lourdes Egydio Villela, a former billionaire, transferred her shares of parent company Itausa to Ricardo and his brother Rodolfo.

name: Anil Gupta
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun India (2016-2019)
forbes_bio: Anil Gupta is the chairman and managing director of Delhi-based power cables manufacturer KEI Industries.
The company's products include stainless steel wires as well as low, medium and high voltage cables.
KEI exports to more than 55 countries across the world.
The company was started in 1968 by his father to make rubber cables for home wiring.
It is also listed on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange.

name: Rulun Huang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2008-2009)
forbes_bio: Huang Rulun leads the Century Golden Resources Group, which has investments in Chinese hotels and shopping malls.
Huang, who was in the trading business in the Philippines in his youth, attended Philippines President Duterte's inauguration ceremony in June 2016.
Huang's son, Huang Tao, has been president of Century Golden Resources Group since 2012.

name: Ryan Graves
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2019-2023)
forbes_bio: Ryan Graves was the first employee hired at ride-hailing service Uber in 2010.
Graves was CEO for a brief period in 2010, then president and most recently SVP of Global Operations, working as a "resident entrepreneur and builder."
He announced he was resigning as an Uber exec in August 2017, two months after cofounder Travis Kalanick was forced to resign as CEO.
Graves left Uber's board in May 2019, a few weeks after its initial public offering; at the time he owned about 2% of the company's shares.
Now, Graves runs private investment firm Saltwater, which acquires small, profitable companies.
forbes_facts: Graves got his job by tweeting at Uber cofounder Travis Kalanick: "here's a tip. email me :)" when Kalanick was looking for a product manager.
Before Uber, Graves worked at GE and was an unpaid intern at Foursquare.

name: David Kong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: David Kong, who also goes by Kong Hon Kong, founded Kuala Lumpur-based Nirvana Asia in 1990 and took it public in Hong Kong in 2014.
Asia's largest death-services provider by sales, it runs private cemeteries, columbarium facilities and funeral homes in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Kong took Nirvana Asia private in 2016 in a $1.1 billion deal with private equity firm CVC Capital Partners.
forbes_facts: The third of ten children, Kong was born to a family of rubber tappers in Kuala Lipis in northern Malaysia.
